description: TinyClaw - Tiny memory infrastructure for AgentHLE, inspired by OpenClaw's memory system. Plain markdown files as source of truth, keyword search, and pre-compaction memory flush.

userStories.title: Understanding Magic Tower - Deep analysis of the task pipeline
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a comprehensive understanding of the Magic Tower task so I can use it as a reference for building new features (e.g., memory infrastructure) and evaluating agent capabilities. Static analysis goes in understanding_magic_tower.txt; live run observations and debug notes go in debug_progress.txt.
acceptanceCriteria: tasks/game/mota_24_easy/understanding_magic_tower.txt exists
File documents the full task lifecycle: task config, setup, agent execution, evaluation
File documents the data flow: how task_description reaches the agent, how screenshots are saved and evaluated
File documents the agent loop: ComputerAgent.run() → step results → usage tracking → DONE detection
File documents the evaluation pipeline: milestone mode, VLM judge, compare_screenshots_game
File documents the shell script invocation: cua_bench.batch.solver CLI args and what they do
File documents environment variables required: VM_IP, OPENAI_API_KEY, CUA_ENV_API_URL, etc.
File documents integration points: where new tools/callbacks can be injected in agenthle_agent.py
File documents the remote VM interaction: session.run_file, session.screenshot, session.interface
grep -c 'ComputerAgent\|perform_task\|evaluate_milestone\|MilestoneTool' tasks/game/mota_24_easy/understanding_magic_tower.txt returns at least 4
userStories.notes: Completed. Static pipeline analysis in understanding_magic_tower.txt, live run observations and debug notes in debug_progress.txt.

userStories.title: MemoryStore - built, integrated into agent, tested with run_magic_tower.sh
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a MemoryStore class that manages MEMORY.md and memory_logs/YYYY-MM-DD.md. It must be integrated into agenthle_agent.py, unit-tested, and validated via run_magic_tower.sh (agent starts and runs without MemoryStore errors).
acceptanceCriteria: memory/store.py exists with MemoryStore class
MemoryStore.__init__ accepts a base_dir path
read_file returns content with correct line ranges; returns empty string for missing files (no exception)
append_to_daily_log creates memory_logs/ dir and file if absent, appends with timestamp
write_memory creates or overwrites MEMORY.md
search does case-insensitive substring matching across all markdown files, returns file path, line number, content, score
list_log_files returns sorted paths of existing daily log files
memory/__init__.py exports MemoryStore
agenthle_agent.py imports MemoryStore and creates an instance in perform_task (base_dir defaults to memory_data/ relative to project root)
uv run pytest tests/test_memory_store.py passes (covers all MemoryStore methods with tmp_path)
run_magic_tower.sh starts without import or instantiation errors from MemoryStore (agent initializes and begins execution)
Lint passes (uv run ruff check .)

userStories.title: memory_search tool - built, wired into agent, tested with run_magic_tower.sh
userStories.description: As an agent, I want a memory_search tool so I can search my memory files using keywords. The tool must be wired into ComputerAgent tools= list, unit-tested, and validated via run_magic_tower.sh (agent has memory_search available and can invoke it).
acceptanceCriteria: memory/tools.py exists with MemorySearchTool class extending BaseTool (from agent.tools.base)
MemorySearchTool registered with @register_tool('memory_search')
Accepts keywords (list of strings) and optional max_results (int) parameters
Delegates to MemoryStore.search() and returns results with file path, line number, matched content
Returns helpful message when no results found
memory/__init__.py exports MemorySearchTool
agenthle_agent.py instantiates MemorySearchTool(store) and adds it to ComputerAgent tools= list
Agent instructions in agenthle_agent.py describe memory_search and when to use it
uv run pytest tests/test_memory_tools.py::test_search passes (unit: seeded MemoryStore, correct results)
run_magic_tower.sh shows memory_search in the agent's available tools and agent runs without tool registration errors
Lint passes (uv run ruff check .)

userStories.title: memory_get tool - built, wired into agent, tested with run_magic_tower.sh
userStories.description: As an agent, I want a memory_get tool so I can read a specific memory file or line range. The tool must be wired into ComputerAgent tools= list, unit-tested, and validated via run_magic_tower.sh (agent has memory_get available and can invoke it).
acceptanceCriteria: memory/tools.py contains MemoryGetTool class extending BaseTool (from agent.tools.base)
MemoryGetTool registered with @register_tool('memory_get')
Accepts file_path (string), optional start_line and end_line (int) parameters
Restricts file_path to MEMORY.md and memory_logs/ (rejects path traversal with ..)
Returns empty string with message for missing files (no exception)
memory/__init__.py exports MemoryGetTool
agenthle_agent.py instantiates MemoryGetTool(store) and adds it to ComputerAgent tools= list
Agent instructions in agenthle_agent.py describe memory_get and when to use it
uv run pytest tests/test_memory_tools.py::test_get passes (unit: read MEMORY.md full + line range, read daily log, path traversal rejected)
run_magic_tower.sh shows memory_get in the agent's available tools and agent runs without tool registration errors
Lint passes (uv run ruff check .)

userStories.title: MemoryFlushCallback - built, registered in agent, tested with run_magic_tower.sh
userStories.description: As a system operator, I want a callback that periodically reminds the agent to save observations to memory and auto-appends a summary at end of run. The callback must be registered in ComputerAgent callbacks= list, unit-tested, and validated via run_magic_tower.sh (callback fires during a live run).
acceptanceCriteria: memory/callback.py exists with MemoryFlushCallback extending AsyncCallbackHandler (from agent.callbacks.base)
Tracks step count; every flush_interval steps, appends a memory flush reminder to messages via on_llm_start
on_run_end appends a summary line to the daily log with task description and step count
Does not crash if memory_logs/ directory does not exist (creates it)
memory/__init__.py exports MemoryFlushCallback
agenthle_agent.py instantiates MemoryFlushCallback(store) and passes it in ComputerAgent callbacks= list
uv run pytest tests/test_memory_callback.py passes (unit: flush reminder at correct intervals, on_run_end writes daily log)
run_magic_tower.sh completes and memory_data/memory_logs/ contains a daily log file with a run summary entry from the callback
Lint passes (uv run ruff check .)

userStories.title: End-to-end memory system validation
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a comprehensive end-to-end test that exercises all memory features together (MemoryStore, memory_search, memory_get, MemoryFlushCallback) both in pytest and via a full run_magic_tower.sh run, proving the entire memory system works as a cohesive whole.
acceptanceCriteria: tests/test_memory_e2e.py exists: wires all memory components together (same as agenthle_agent.py), seeds data, exercises search/get/callback in sequence, verifies shared MemoryStore state across components
uv run pytest tests/test_memory_e2e.py -v passes
run_magic_tower.sh completes a full run: agent uses memory_search and memory_get tools (visible in trajectory logs), MemoryFlushCallback fires and creates daily log entries
After run_magic_tower.sh, memory_data/memory_logs/ contains at least one daily log with run summary, and memory_data/MEMORY.md exists if agent wrote to it
uv run python -c 'from memory import MemoryStore, MemorySearchTool, MemoryGetTool, MemoryFlushCallback' succeeds
Lint passes (uv run ruff check .)
userStories.notes: Final validation story. Each feature is already individually integrated and tested in US-MEM-001 through US-MEM-004. The run_magic_tower.sh test requires a running VM (VM_IP set).
